title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-06
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: 인사팀 전 미싱사 연락 명단 오전 회수, 본사 조직도 리컨펌 아침 회신, 금요일 주간 보고 2건, 회계에 보험 재제안 일정 확인
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Tomorrow is Friday, November sixth. This is your English briefing for Friday.
Friday is a busy day. You have two weekly reports, a few lists to collect, and some replies to send. Let's get ready together.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three for Friday. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is a short practice of key sentences. Part eight is the closing. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for Friday.
Number one. The list of former sewers from the HR manager.

What is it? We want to hire more sewers by next spring. One idea is to call sewers who left the company before. the HR manager is preparing a list of former sewers. On Thursday afternoon, you asked her to send the list by Friday morning. The list must show who to exclude, and the missing phone numbers must be filled in.

the HR manager replied at about four PM. She said they added more phone numbers. But she said the formula did not work. She used your formula for the "Exclude" column, but it did not show the Zalo number.

Why is it important? A head office manager asked about the drop in sewers on Thursday. You already replied with the reasons and the plan. The call list is the first real step of that plan. If the list is late, the whole plan is late.

Your first action on Friday. Open the file from the HR manager. Look at the "Exclude" column and the Zalo column. Fix the formula, or show her how to fix it. Then confirm the final count of people to call. Remember one more thing. Before we call them, we must be sure we may use their phone numbers.
Number two. The fire insurance renewal.

What is it? Head office, a head office manager, needs a report for the CEO by November eleventh. The report must show two options, six months and one year. On Thursday, the accountant sent revised figures twice. Then you rebuilt the sum insured yourself and sent her the file with a "Basis" sheet. Building and machinery use the original cost. Office items and tools use the book value. Stock uses the actual stock on the cut-off date.
the accountant also said one thing. We must wait for the insurance broker, to send a new proposal. Only then will we know the support rate for fire protection equipment.
Why is it important? The deadline is next Wednesday. Your own target is Tuesday, November tenth. If the broker is slow, you will run out of time.

Your first action on Friday. Ask the accountant if she has sent your new figures to the broker. Ask when the broker will send the revised proposal. Also check that the premium for each option is in US dollars, with and without VAT.
Number three. The two Friday weekly reports.
What are they? The first one is the weekly outsourcing usage report to my director. The second one is the weekly cash report to head office finance.

Why is it important? These two come every Friday. They are easy to forget when the day is busy. The outsourcing report is more sensitive this week. On Thursday, head office asked about outsourcing and customs. You replied that there was no outsourcing work without a customs declaration. So the weekly report must match what you told head office.
Your first action on Friday. In the morning, check the outsourcing form for new work since last Friday. In the afternoon, prepare the cash report after the accounting team confirms the numbers.
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, the HR manager. As we said, you need the final call list of former sewers. Check the "Exclude" mark and the phone numbers. Also ask about her opinion on the sewing challenge video scripts. The preparation for the video is due on Saturday.
Here is a sentence you can use. "the HR manager, could you send me the final list by eleven AM? Please mark Exclude for each person."

Second, the maintenance leader. On Thursday, you asked him to check every electrical panel, socket and power strip in the factory. He must fill in the fire patch status in the file. Head office needs our answer by Monday, November ninth. So you need his file by Saturday at the latest.
Here is a sentence you can use. "the maintenance leader, when will you be able to send the fire patch file? I need it by Saturday noon."

Third, the purchasing staff. She still owes you three things. One, the October electricity VAT invoices and the October water invoice. Two, the consumables ledger. Three, quotations for three whiteboards from two suppliers, by Saturday. The invoices and the ledger are already late. Remember, she is a person to watch closely.
Here is a sentence you can use. "Hi, just a reminder that the October invoices are already late. Please upload them by ten AM today."

Fourth, the compliance officer. She owes you a lab test result. It was due on October thirty-first. Also, on Thursday you asked her a new question. Can we use the fire protection support fee for a jockey pump? A jockey pump keeps the pressure in the fire water pipes.
Here is a sentence you can use. "the compliance officer, as far as I can see, the lab test result is still missing. When will you be able to send it?"

Fifth, the accountant. She owes you the fire insurance update. She also owes you two answers on the October purchase cost list. You already sent the list to head office on Thursday, so check her answers match.
Here is a sentence you can use. "the accountant, please keep me posted on the the broker proposal until it arrives."
Part three. Replies I owe.

First, A head office manager, about the organization chart. On Thursday at about four PM, the IT staff sent his update. He said there are no staff changes in November. He also sent screenshots. Your reply to the head office manager was due on Thursday. So send it first thing on Friday, after you check the screenshots.
A first sentence for your reply. "Dear Ms the head office manager, I have checked the organization chart for November, and there are no staff changes."

Second, the head office manager at head office, about the fire patches. He asked every factory to buy and attach fire patches by itself. The deadline is Monday, November ninth. You will answer after the maintenance leader sends his file.
A first sentence for your reply. "Dear Sir, we checked all panels and sockets in the factory, and here is our purchase plan by priority."

Third, a head office manager at head office, about the new purchase approval rule. He asked whether any Danang items were missing from this week's list. He will report to the CEO on Friday, November sixth. Please check this early on Friday morning.
A first sentence for your reply. "Dear the head office manager, I checked this week's list, and no Danang items are missing."

Fourth, my director. Two items are still open. One, the result of the sewer grade test idea, after the factory manager checks it. Two, the result of the broken pallet disposal, with the weight ticket and the invoice. If you can, report both in one short message on Friday.
A first sentence for your report. "my director, I'd like to update you on two items: the sewer grade test and the pallet disposal."

Fifth, the compliance officer, about two older questions. One is the lunch time sewing rule for a buyer audit. The other is the battery recycling event on November twenty-seventh. She is waiting for your approval.
A first sentence for your reply. "the compliance officer, sorry for the late reply. Here is my answer on the lunch time work and the battery event."
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.

Friday, November sixth. The weekly outsourcing usage report to my director. The weekly cash report to head office finance. The call list from the HR manager in the morning. the head office manager reports to the CEO on the purchase approval rule.

Saturday, November seventh. At eight AM, the payroll report is on your calendar. The whiteboard quotations from the purchasing staff are due. The video preparation is due, including the coach and the consent forms.
Sunday, November eighth. The contractor will tighten the cable lugs in the electrical cabinets. Remember, payment only after the cabinet temperatures are normal.
Monday, November ninth. The weekly firewood report. The fire patch answer to the head office manager is due at the end of the working day.
Wednesday, November eleventh. The fire insurance report to head office. Your own target is Tuesday.
Part five. English review.
Let's review nine expressions from Thursday, Wednesday, last Monday, and last Thursday. Two of them were wrong on your last test, so we will practice them well.

The first expression is "withhold." It means to hold back a payment or an approval for now. For example, "We will withhold payment until the cabinet temperatures are confirmed normal." Now say it with me.
We will withhold payment until the cabinet temperatures are confirmed normal. ... ... ...
One more time. We will withhold payment. ... ... ...
The second expression is "premium." For insurance, it means the money you pay for the policy. For example, "Please send me the premium for the six-month and one-year options." Now say it with me.
Please send me the premium for the six-month and one-year options. ... ... ...
One more time. Please send me the premium. ... ... ...

The third expression is "Payment will be made only once" something happens. It means we pay only after a condition is met. For example, "Payment will be made only once all cabinets show normal temperatures." Now say it with me.
Payment will be made only once all cabinets show normal temperatures. ... ... ...
One more time. Payment will be made only once the work is checked. ... ... ...

The fourth expression is "If that's not possible, please check whether" something. It gives a second choice. For example, "If that's not possible, please check whether we can rent a thermal camera." Now say it with me.
If that's not possible, please check whether we can rent a thermal camera. ... ... ...
One more time. If that's not possible, please check whether we can rent one. ... ... ...

The fifth expression is "consent." It means a person says yes to something, for example to the use of their personal data. For example, "We will call the sewers only after we get their consent to use their phone numbers." This one is very useful for Friday. Now say it with me.
We will call the sewers only after we get their consent. ... ... ...
One more time. We need their consent first. ... ... ...

The sixth expression is "I'll get back to you on" something. It means I will answer that part later. For example, "I'll get back to you on the support rate after the broker sends the new proposal." Now say it with me.
I'll get back to you on the support rate. ... ... ...
One more time. I'll get back to you on that by Monday. ... ... ...
The seventh expression is "As far as I can see." It means "from what I checked." For example, "As far as I can see, the October invoices are still not in the folder." Now say it with me.
As far as I can see, the October invoices are still not in the folder. ... ... ...
One more time. As far as I can see, it is still missing. ... ... ...

The eighth expression is "prioritize." You got this wrong on the last test. It means to do something first because it is more important. For example, "Please prioritize the new building and the warehouses for the fire patches." Now say it with me.
Please prioritize the new building and the warehouses. ... ... ...
One more time. Please prioritize this today. ... ... ...
The ninth expression is "When will you be able to" do something. It is a soft way to ask for a date. For example, "When will you be able to send the final list?" Now say it with me.
When will you be able to send the final list? ... ... ...
One more time. When will you be able to send it? ... ... ...
Part six. A short role-play.
This is Friday morning. Anthony calls the HR manager about the call list of former sewers.
Anthony: Good morning, the HR manager. I saw your mail about the formula. Do you have a minute?
HR manager: Good morning, Mr Lee. Yes. We added more phone numbers, but the Zalo number does not show.
Anthony: I see. The formula looks at the old phone column. Your new numbers are in a new column, right?
HR manager: Yes, that's right. We put them in a new column.
Anthony: OK. Please put all phone numbers in one column. Then the formula will work. I will check it with you after that.
HR manager: Thank you. How many people should we exclude?
Anthony: Please use the rule we agreed on. If we should not call a person again, mark "Yes" in the Exclude column.
HR manager: OK. We can finish it by eleven AM.
Anthony: Great. One more thing. Before we call them, we need their consent to use their phone numbers. Please prepare a short opening sentence for the call. The person must agree first.
HR manager: I understand. I will send you the sentence with the list.
Anthony: Thank you. When will you be able to start the calls?
HR manager: We can start on Monday, if you approve the list today.
Anthony: Good. I'll get back to you on the list by three PM today.
Now let's practice two key sentences from the role-play.
Sentence one. "Before we call them, we need their consent to use their phone numbers." Say it with me.
Before we call them, we need their consent to use their phone numbers. ... ... ...
One more time. Before we call them, we need their consent. ... ... ...
Sentence two. "I'll get back to you on the list by three PM today." Say it with me.
I'll get back to you on the list by three PM today. ... ... ...
One more time. I'll get back to you on the list by three PM. ... ... ...
Part seven. A short practice of key sentences for Friday.
Here are four more sentences you will use on Friday. Listen and repeat.
For the head office manager. "I have checked the organization chart, and there are no staff changes in November." ... ... ...
For the accountant. "Please keep me posted on the the broker proposal until it arrives." ... ... ...
For the purchasing staff. "Just a reminder that the October invoices are already late." ... ... ...
For the maintenance leader. "Please prioritize the new building and the warehouses." ... ... ...
Let's say the most important one again. "Before we call them, we need their consent." ... ... ...
Part eight. Closing.

Here is the one thing to do on Friday. Get the final call list from the HR manager by eleven AM, and reply to the head office manager on the organization chart first thing in the morning. Then finish the two weekly reports before you go home.
You did a lot on Thursday. Friday is the last push before the weekend. Have a safe ride, and good luck, Anthony. See you on Saturday.
